description: Stress-scenario calibration data (§2.8, §4.9). This pipeline pulls only the stress-SPECIFIC inputs that are not already a per-asset-class market input: broad credit-spread indices (FRED IG/HY OAS), the equity- and rates-vol level series (FRED VIXCLS, Yahoo ^MOVE) and datacenter power demand (EIA). Hyperscaler capex (EDGAR XBRL) lives in the reference pipeline; single-name CDS in credit; equity prices + CBOE VIX/skew archives in equity/options; UST curve in bonds. Scope of THIS stage: Methodology B (AI capex boom/bust). Methodology A (historical replay) and its BIS FX/funding history + episode-window scenario generation are a later stage (see notes). See docs/design/AITrade_quantlib_portfolio_marketdata.md §2.8, §4.9.

scenario_scope.methodology_B: AI capex boom/bust (thematic, forward-looking) — §4.9. Built bottom-up: (1) capex run-rate + YoY from EDGAR XBRL [reference pipeline], (2) corroborated by EIA datacenter power demand YoY [eia_power below], (3) bust legs sized as ΔOAS [fred_macro BAMLC0A0CM/HY], ΔVIX [fred_macro VIXCLS + CBOE archive], ΔMOVE [move_yahoo], equity drawdown [equity prices], CDS widening [credit pipeline], UST flight-to-quality [bonds].
scenario_scope.methodology_A_deferred: Historical replay (GFC/Euro/China-deval/COVID/2022) is NOT built in this stage. Its extra source pulls — BIS WS_XRU / WS_EER / WS_GLI / WS_OTC_DERIV2 bulk files (FX devaluation paths + USD funding squeeze) — and the peak-to-trough episode-window shock-vector generation are deferred. The Taiwan joint-tail (Methodology B step 4) also depends on BIS WS_XRU and is deferred with it.

factor_map.fred_BAMLC0A0CM: IG corp OAS — credit-spread widening for bonds #15-19, CDS #28-30 (primary B credit leg)
factor_map.fred_BAMLH0A0HYM2: HY corp OAS — risk-appetite tail (Methodology A scale; carried here for the bust HY overlay)
factor_map.fred_BAA10Y: Baa-10Y spread — free long-history credit proxy backfilling the IG-OAS VaR factor before its ~3y FRED start (risk Tier 1.1)
factor_map.fred_AAA10Y: Aaa-10Y spread — free long-history high-grade credit proxy (alternate backfill source)
factor_map.fred_VIXCLS: Equity implied-vol spike — vega shock for options #7-14, delta for equity #1-6 (daily close; CBOE VIX_History.csv in options/ is the intraday-high archive)
factor_map.yahoo_MOVE: Rates implied-vol spike — swaption vega #23-24, cap #25
factor_map.eia_demand: Datacenter power-load growth — independent AI-capex corroboration (semis #1/#3/#4, hyperscaler bonds #16-19)

notes: Scenario DEFINITIONS refresh quarterly (after EDGAR capex + EIA demand update); the weekly run only re-applies stored shock vectors to the latest curves (§4.9 cadence note).
8-year lookback from 2018 aligns with the equity/reference windows and spans the pre-AI-capex baseline, COVID, the 2022 rate shock and the GPU-capex boom — enough to size the bust shocks.
FRED OAS/VIX and ^MOVE are daily; EIA demand is resampled to daily (see eia_power.frequency). EIA region-data starts 2019 (eia_power.start_date_override).

fred_macro.name: FRED — credit-spread (OAS) + equity-vol stress indices
fred_macro.description: ICE BofA IG/HY option-adjusted spreads and VIX close via the fredgraph.csv endpoint (no API key, avoids the /fred/series 504). BAMLC0A0CM is the ΔOAS scalar for the bust credit leg; BAMLH0A0HYM2 the HY risk-appetite tail; VIXCLS the daily equity-vol level (CBOE VIX_History.csv in options/vol_indices is the authoritative intraday-high archive — VIXCLS is the close aligned to the OAS series for joint scaling). OAS units are PERCENT (0.75 = 75 bps).
fred_macro.data_limitation: FRED now serves only a ROLLING ~3-YEAR window for the proprietary ICE BofA OAS series (BAMLC0A0CM/BAMLH0A0HYM2 start ~3y back, e.g. 2023-06; confirmed on both fredgraph.csv AND the keyed /fred/series/observations API — it is an ICE licensing restriction, not an endpoint issue). This trailing window covers the AI-capex boom and current spread levels/vol — sufficient to size Methodology B bust shocks relative to today. Full COVID/2022/GFC OAS history (needed for Methodology A historical-replay ΔOAS anchors) is NOT free from FRED and is deferred to the Methodology A stage (candidate alternatives: NBER/St Louis archived snapshots, or a licensed ICE/Markit feed). VIXCLS is NOT ICE-licensed and returns full history (1990-present).

series.BAMLC0A0CM: ICE BofA US IG corporate OAS (percent; 0.75 = 75 bps); primary credit-spread shock for bonds #15-19 and CDS #28-30 [~3y rolling window — see data_limitation]
series.BAMLH0A0HYM2: ICE BofA US HY OAS (percent); risk-appetite tail overlay [~3y rolling window]
series.VIXCLS: CBOE VIX close; equity implied-vol spike for options #7-14 vega [full history]
series.BAA10Y: Moody's Baa corporate yield minus 10Y Treasury (percent); FREE LONG-HISTORY credit-spread proxy, daily since 1986, NOT ICE-licensed. Used by the risk engine (Tier 1.1) to backfill the IG-OAS credit factor before its ~3y FRED start so the credit factor stops throttling the aligned VaR window [full history]
series.AAA10Y: Moody's Aaa corporate yield minus 10Y Treasury (percent); free long-history high-grade credit-spread proxy, daily since 1983 [full history; carried as an alternate/AAA backfill source]

move_yahoo.name: Yahoo Finance — ICE BofAML MOVE index (rates implied vol)
move_yahoo.description: ^MOVE daily history — the rates-vol level for the swaption/cap vega shock (#23-25). MOVE is not free on FRED; Yahoo's chart endpoint requires a real browser User-Agent (bare requests get HTTP 401). Same parser shape as the equity Yahoo downloader.

extra_headers.User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

eia_power.name: EIA v2 — datacenter-grid electricity demand (AI-capex corroboration)
eia_power.description: Daily electricity demand (type=D) for the datacenter-heavy balancing authorities — PJM (N. Virginia 'Data Center Alley'), ERCO (Texas), MISO, CISO. YoY growth in regional baseload independently corroborates/contradicts hyperscaler capex guidance (§4.9 Methodology B step 2): rising load that leads capex confirms the buildout; flattening load is an early bust signal, and grid interconnection limits are the binding physical constraint. Requires a FREE EIA API key (instant signup at eia.gov/opendata) supplied IN the query string via EIA_API_KEY; if unset the source logs a warning and is skipped (no crash). Default route is the daily-region-data series (YoY-baseload appropriate, ~365 rows/yr/region); the design's hourly region-data route is available by swapping endpoint_path + frequency.
eia_power.timezone_note: daily-region-data buckets the hourly series into calendar days per timezone, returning 5 near-identical rows (~0.1% apart) per (date,respondent) — one per tz boundary (Pacific/Central/Mountain/Eastern/Arizona; no UTC). We request each respondent in ITS LOCAL timezone so the value is the true local-calendar-day demand and there is exactly one row per (date,respondent).

gpr.name: Geopolitical Risk index (Caldara-Iacoviello) — F8
gpr.description: Daily GLOBAL GPR (GPRD/acts/threats) + MONTHLY country sub-indices (GPRC_TWN/GPRC_CHN). Gives taiwan_geopolitical a quantitative trigger + severity calibration (FINDING 8). Country sub-indices are monthly (the daily file is global only), so both files are ingested. Binary .xls parsed via BytesIO (trap 2).

fred_throughput.name: FRED semiconductor industrial production — F9
fred_throughput.description: IPG3344S (semiconductor & related-device manufacturing industrial production) — a PHYSICAL corroboration of the AI-capex thesis. scenariogen reads it (with EIA datacenter power demand) as a throughput severity multiplier on ai_bust: decelerating throughput amplifies the bust. Separate file from fred_stress_macro.csv (stays out of the credit factor's file). Same fredgraph.csv path, no key.

epu.name: Economic Policy Uncertainty — daily US (F8)
epu.description: Baker-Bloom-Davis daily US policy-uncertainty index (graceful context alongside GPR). Plain CSV, no key.

fred_long.name: FRED — long rates / VIX / credit / FX history (severity anchors)
fred_long.description: Full-history fredgraph.csv series from 1990 for the scenario severity anchors (docs/design/scenario_set_and_ablation_design.md §3.3): Treasury yields (percent), VIXCLS (index points), Moody's BAA10Y (percent; the FREE long credit proxy — ICE BofA OAS is only served ~3y back, see fred_macro.data_limitation) and FX (DEXJPUS JPY per USD, DEXTAUS TWD per USD). Writes its OWN wide file; fred_stress_macro.csv and fred_rates.csv (VaR / pricing inputs) are untouched.
